Container.Name: print-handy
Container.Overview: Print Handy Discord bot, Moonraker listener, OrcaSlicer and the bundled Spoolman API in one supervised container. Includes the alert-only camera watchdog: spaghetti, detached-part, empty-bed and stall checks post a camera photo to Discord (tune it with the Camera watch variables). Timelapse capture is off by default: set the Timelapse capture variable below to record timelapses inside the container (a camera source for your printer family is required; the optional SSH timelapse archive in the config file is a separate thing and is never required for capture or delivery). Print Handy is the interface; Spoolman's web UI is not included. The Spoolman API listens on 127.0.0.1:8000 inside the container and no port is published by default; the advanced Spoolman port and SPOOLMAN_HOST fields below expose it on the LAN only when you opt in (#443). The Web UI (simple status plus picker configuration that syncs to the YAML settings) is enabled by this template so the WebUI link above works — but it only starts once the Web UI access token below is set, because the template binds it on all interfaces; without a token it stays off and the container log says why (#440). Printers are external services. UPGRADE NOTE — this project was renamed from Print Buddy to Print Handy, and this template is a NEW Community Applications app (the old one was print-buddy): existing Print Buddy installs do not auto-migrate. Install this template, copy your old appdata (/mnt/user/appdata/print-buddy) into the new print-handy appdata paths (renaming any print_buddy_* state files to print_handy_*), move the configuration values across from the old PRINT_BUDDY__... names to the new PRINT_HANDY__... variable names, start this container and check it is healthy, then remove the old app. Full steps are in docs/RENAME-MIGRATION.md in the project repo.
Container.ExtraParams: --user 1000:1000 --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges:true --shm-size 256m --log-driver json-file --log-opt max-size=10m --log-opt max-file=3 --restart unless-stopped --health-cmd "python3 /usr/local/bin/print-handy-healthcheck" --health-interval 30s --health-timeout 10s --health-start-period 90s --health-retries 3
Container.Requires: Appdata paths owned by UID/GID 1000. Existing Spoolman data can be copied into the Spoolman Data path before first start; nothing is migrated automatically.

Config.Name: State
Config.Description: Runtime state, prompts, hardware and job records. Back this up.

Config.Name: Archive
Config.Description: Sliced jobs and G-code. Back this up.

Config.Name: Records
Config.Description: Print records. Back this up.

Config.Name: Cache
Config.Description: Regenerable cache.

Config.Name: Spoolman data
Config.Description: Bundled Spoolman database, config, logs and backups. Back this up.

Config.Name: Account tokens
Config.Description: OPTIONAL. Account tokens for model sites (MakerWorld, Thingiverse and others), kept outside the container so they survive recreation. Create the folder and make it owned by 1000:1000 first; see docs/DOCKER.md.

Config.Name: Web UI port
Config.Description: Container port of the Web UI, so the WebUI link works (PRINT_HANDY__WEBUI__PORT must match this port). While the Web UI is disabled below, nothing answers on it.

Config.Name: Spoolman port
Config.Description: OPTIONAL, LAN only (#443): publishes the bundled Spoolman API (container port 8000) so Moonraker on printer hardware (for example a ZMod AD5X) and Home Assistant can reach it at http://[unraid-ip]:7912. Leave this mapping deleted to keep Spoolman loopback-only inside the container. Publishing it also requires SPOOLMAN_HOST=0.0.0.0 below, or Spoolman still refuses the connection. The API is unauthenticated: never forward this port from a router.

Config.Name: Settings file
Config.Description: Leave as is, or point at a mounted YAML file for list settings.

Config.Name: Bot mode
Config.Description: Must be standalone in Docker.

Config.Name: Discord bot token
Config.Description: Secret. Leave empty to stage the listener and Spoolman without the Discord bot.

Config.Name: Discord channel ID
Config.Description: Channel Print Handy uses.

Config.Name: Allowed user IDs
Config.Description: Optional whitelist of Discord user IDs allowed to use the bot, comma or space separated. Leave empty (the default) and everyone who can post in the print channel can use the bot — the channel is the access boundary.

Config.Name: Denied user IDs
Config.Description: Optional deny list of Discord user IDs, comma or space separated. A denied user is refused even when whitelisted or the approval user; a refusal is logged and answered once per user per hour.

Config.Name: Discord approval user ID
Config.Description: Discord user ID allowed to approve prints; always allowed to use the bot as well. Empty leaves approvals to the allowed users (or, with no whitelist, the channel).

Config.Name: Discord timezone
Config.Description: IANA timezone for display times and the daily session reset, for example America/New_York. Separate from the container timezone below.

Config.Name: Printer model
Config.Description: flashforge.ad5x, flashforge.ad5m, flashforge.ad5m_pro, flashforge.creator5, flashforge.creator5_pro, sovol.sv06, klipper.generic, octoprint.marlin, bambulab.a1 or bambulab.p1s (Bambu Lab models are offline only).

Config.Name: Moonraker URL
Config.Description: Klipper printers, for example http://printer.example:7125. Fluidd is not needed here.

Config.Name: Moonraker API key
Config.Description: Secret, only when Moonraker requires an API key.

Config.Name: Flashforge stock LAN host
Config.Description: Stock Flashforge printer LAN address for IFS presence and screen-error alerts. Empty leaves the printer offline; set it together with the serial and check code below.

Config.Name: Flashforge serial
Config.Description: Secret. The stock printer serial number; never a setting in a config file.

Config.Name: Flashforge check code
Config.Description: Secret. The stock printer check code; never a setting in a config file.

Config.Name: Bambu LAN host
Config.Description: Bambu Lab printers: LAN address for read-only status, plain host with no scheme or port. Set it together with the Bambu serial below; empty disables LAN status.

Config.Name: Bambu serial
Config.Description: Bambu Lab printers: the printer serial number for read-only LAN status. Set it together with the Bambu LAN host.

Config.Name: Bambu LAN access code
Config.Description: Secret. The Bambu Lab printer LAN access code for read-only status; never a setting in a config file.

Config.Name: OctoPrint URL
Config.Description: octoprint.marlin printers only.

Config.Name: OctoPrint API key
Config.Description: Secret, octoprint.marlin printers only.

Config.Name: Spoolman URL
Config.Description: Bundled Spoolman API by default. To use an existing external Spoolman, set its URL here and set Bundled Spoolman to false; nothing is migrated.

Config.Name: Bundled Spoolman
Config.Description: true runs the bundled Spoolman API; false uses the external Spoolman URL.

Config.Name: Spoolman bind host
Config.Description: Host the bundled Spoolman API binds to inside the container (#443). Default 127.0.0.1 keeps it loopback-only and unexposed, even with the Spoolman port mapping above present. Set 0.0.0.0 ONLY when you publish the Spoolman port for LAN Moonraker (printer hardware) or Home Assistant access; the API is unauthenticated, so keep it on the LAN and never forward it from a router.

Config.Name: OrcaSlicer channel
Config.Description: Bundled OrcaSlicer channel selected at startup: stable (default) or preview. alpha, the old name for preview, is still accepted for now. Any other value stops the container at startup.

Config.Name: Camera watch
Config.Description: Camera watchdog: posts a Discord photo alert for spaghetti, a detached part, an empty bed or a stalled print. Alert only; it never controls the printer. Needs a camera snapshot and a vision endpoint (see docs/DOCKER.md).

Config.Name: Camera watch sensitivity
Config.Description: How readily the camera watchdog alerts, 1 (quietest) to 5 (most alerts). 3 is the original behavior; periodic checks run every 30, 20, 15, 10 or 7.5 minutes for levels 1 to 5.

Config.Name: Vision chat URL
Config.Description: OpenAI-compatible endpoint for camera checks and roasts. Empty disables both; set it together with the vision API key below.

Config.Name: Camera snapshot URL
Config.Description: Camera snapshot URL for the camera watchdog. Empty derives it from the Moonraker host.

Config.Name: Timelapse capture
Config.Description: In-container timelapse capture (#246): starts the bundled go2rtc to normalise the camera source on loopback. Off by default and opt-in; off keeps the printer-rendered timelapse behaviour. This variable is an environment override: when set it wins over timelapse.capture_enabled in a mounted config file. Capture needs a camera source for your printer family (a Moonraker webcam, Bambu stills or X1 RTSPS stream, a PrusaLink-registered camera, or an AD5X accessory camera; Elegoo SDCP has no verified camera source yet — see docs/DOCKER.md). Separate from the optional SSH timelapse archive (timelapse.archive_host / archive_dir in the config file): that only archives printer-rendered videos and is never required for capture or for a video to be attached. go2rtc's API/RTSP stay on loopback and are never published.

Config.Name: Timelapse capture source
Config.Description: Optional explicit capture camera source (MJPEG/RTSP URL or a go2rtc ffmpeg: source). Empty derives it from the camera snapshot URL / Moonraker webcam. A URL here may carry camera credentials; it is written only to the generated go2rtc config (0600) inside the container.

Config.Name: Timelapse capture trigger
Config.Description: Stage 2 frame capture trigger (#246): interval (a frame every capture interval), layer (a frame on each layer change), or both.

Config.Name: Timelapse capture interval (s)
Config.Description: Seconds between captured frames for the interval trigger (#246 stage 2).

Config.Name: Timelapse capture max frames
Config.Description: Per-job cap on captured frames (#246 stage 2); 0 disables the cap.

Config.Name: Timelapse capture max bytes
Config.Description: Per-job cap on captured frame bytes (#246 stage 2); 0 disables the cap.

Config.Name: Timelapse capture encoder
Config.Description: Encoder preference for the Stage 3 timelapse encode (#246): auto, vaapi, nvenc, qsv or cpu. Capture itself never encodes.

Config.Name: Vision model
Config.Description: Model the vision endpoint uses for camera checks.

Config.Name: Roast
Config.Description: The one-line roast added to print-started and print-complete posts. On by default: it runs whenever an LLM/vision endpoint is available (the vision chat URL and API key above), on every platform, Telegram included. Set false to turn roasts off; camera checks keep working either way.

Config.Name: Local failure detector
Config.Description: Built-in ONNX failure detector for the camera watchdog (#455): judges camera frames on this machine when no vision endpoint is configured, so a no-LLM, no-cloud install still gets bad-print detection. Off by default. The pinned model (Obico failure detector, about 202 MB) downloads once into the Hermes home and is SHA-256 verified. It detects failures only; the empty-plate check, roasts and label reads still need a vision endpoint.

Config.Name: Local detector model path
Config.Description: Path to the local failure detector's ONNX model file. Empty uses the default location (a models folder under the Hermes home) and the pinned model; set it to a model file you placed yourself to run fully offline.

Config.Name: Auto light-off minutes
Config.Description: Auto light-off (#516): the printer light turns on when a print starts and off again after the plate has been seen empty for this many minutes. 0 = off (the default). Needs a vision endpoint, like the camera watchdog. 30 is the suggested value.

Config.Name: Light object
Config.Description: The Moonraker light object the auto light-off switches, for example 'led chamber_led', 'neopixel sb_leds' or 'output_pin caselight'. Leave empty to auto-discover: the printer's light object is used only when there is exactly one.

Config.Name: Ask brand for new spools
Config.Description: Ask for the brand/vendor during the conversational new-spool walkthrough (#512). Off by default: the walkthrough skips brand and the spool is created without one. Set true if you track brands.

Config.Name: Vision API key
Config.Description: Secret. Key for the vision chat URL above.

Config.Name: Discord chat LLM
Config.Description: Free-text chat replies from the LLM below on Discord. On by default. Set false to run Discord as a pure bot: unmatched text gets the short not-understood reply, while the LLM stays configured for /print-design (which inherits it). Roasts and camera checks keep their own vision settings either way.

Config.Name: LLM chat URL
Config.Description: Optional OpenAI-compatible chat URL for standalone free-text replies. Empty means unmatched text gets the command list; set it together with the LLM model and key below.

Config.Name: LLM model
Config.Description: LLM model name, required when the LLM chat URL is set.

Config.Name: MakerWorld token
Config.Description: Secret, optional. MakerWorld account token (the token cookie). A file in /data/.config/bambu/token wins over this.

Config.Name: Thingiverse App Token
Config.Description: Secret, optional. Thingiverse App Token from your app at thingiverse.com/developers. A file in /data/.config/thingiverse/token wins over this.

Config.Name: Cults3D API key
Config.Description: Secret, optional. Cults3D nickname:key (listing only; Cults never shares files). A file in /data/.config/cults3d/token wins over this.

Config.Name: Creality Cloud token
Config.Description: Secret, optional. Creality Cloud login for downloads, written model_user_id:model_token (both cookie values). A token file in /data/.config/crealitycloud/token wins over this; the bot's Connect account button explains both.

Config.Name: Thangs token
Config.Description: Secret, optional. Thangs login token (the accessToken value) for downloads. Lasts about 7 days. A token file in /data/.config/thangs/token wins over this.

Config.Name: Nexprint token
Config.Description: Secret, optional. Nexprint login token (the auth_token cookie) for downloads. A token file in /data/.config/nexprint/token wins over this.

Config.Name: MyMiniFactory sign-in
Config.Description: Secret, optional. MyMiniFactory OAuth access token for downloads (see the bot's Connect account steps; lasts about a week). A file in /data/.config/myminifactory/oauth_token wins over this.

Config.Name: LLM API key
Config.Description: Secret. Key for the LLM chat URL above.

Config.Name: Web UI
Config.Description: Web UI (#286, #440): a simple status page plus picker configuration that syncs to the YAML settings file. On by default so the WebUI link works. With the access token below empty it needs no login (anyone on your LAN who can reach the port can use it); set the token to require it. Set false to turn it off entirely; then nothing listens and the Web UI port above answers nothing.

Config.Name: Web UI bind host
Config.Description: Host the Web UI binds to inside the container. The template default 0.0.0.0 makes it reachable through the Web UI port mapping. Use 127.0.0.1 to keep it inside the container.

Config.Name: Web UI port setting
Config.Description: Port the Web UI listens on inside the container; must match the Web UI port mapping above. 0 disables the listener even when the Web UI is enabled.

Config.Name: Web UI access token
Config.Description: Secret, optional. Empty: the Web UI needs no login on your LAN. Set a long random value to require it everywhere: the WebUI link then opens the login page, where you paste this token once to get a browser session; API clients (the Home Assistant integration) send it as the X-WebUI-Token header or Authorization: Bearer. Never a setting in a config file.

Config.Name: Live camera in Discord
Config.Description: Live camera viewing in Discord (#311): an Activity page in the configured voice channel, served by this container through a named Cloudflare Tunnel. Off by default; when true, the fields below, the Discord application ID and both live secrets are all required before the Activity server starts. Setup: docs/DISCORD-BOT-SETUP.md.

Config.Name: Live voice channel ID
Config.Description: The one private Discord voice channel the live Activity is launched in. Keep it limited to your household; the bot never names another channel.

Config.Name: Live auto-start on print
Config.Description: Start the live view automatically when a print starts and post the Activity pointer. Off by default; /print-live start is the manual trigger.

Config.Name: Live feed max height
Config.Description: Live feed height cap in pixels (144-2160); width follows the camera's aspect.

Config.Name: Live feed FPS
Config.Description: Live feed frame-rate cap (1-60).

Config.Name: Live feed max bitrate (kbps)
Config.Description: Live feed bitrate cap in kbit/s (100-20000).

Config.Name: Live feed encoder
Config.Description: Encoder preference for the live feed: auto, vaapi, qsv, nvenc or cpu.

Config.Name: Live empty timeout (s)
Config.Description: Seconds the live view may stay empty of viewers before the session ends itself.

Config.Name: Live Activity origin
Config.Description: Public https origin the Activity page is served from: the named Cloudflare Tunnel's hostname, mapped in the Discord Developer Portal.

Config.Name: Live Activity port
Config.Description: Loopback port the Activity server binds inside the container; the tunnel ingress points here. The settings default is 0 (no port chosen), the template pre-fills 8091 so the tunnel target is fixed; nothing publishes this port.

Config.Name: Discord application ID
Config.Description: The Discord application's ID (a plain identifier from the Developer Portal, not a secret). Required for the live view's OAuth exchange when it is enabled.

Config.Name: Discord client secret
Config.Description: Secret. The Discord application's client secret, used server-side for the live view's OAuth exchange. Never a setting in a config file.

Config.Name: Live session secret
Config.Description: Secret. Signs the live view's Activity session markers; use a long random value. Never a setting in a config file.

Config.Name: Cloudflare Tunnel token
Config.Description: Secret. Token of the named Cloudflare Tunnel for the live view. It belongs to the cloudflared connector you run alongside Print Handy (on Unraid, a separate cloudflared container); Print Handy itself never reads it — the field keeps it beside the other live-view fields.

Config.Name: Container timezone
Config.Description: IANA timezone for the container's local time — log timestamps, scheduled and timed features and the bundled services' timestamps — for example Europe/London. The image default is America/New_York; an unknown name is logged at startup and the default is used. Separate from the Discord display timezone above.
